Libraries
```{r}
library(zoo)
library(forecast)
library(dplyr)
library(Hmisc)
```

EDA
```{r}
df = read.csv("~/STA137-Final-Project/Documents/STA137_Final/Temp_NH_1850_2025.csv", header = FALSE)

colnames(df) <- c("Year", "TempAnomaly")
str(df)
print(paste0("# of NA's: ", sum(is.na(df))))
min(df$TempAnomaly)
max(df$TempAnomaly)
df
# Temp Anomaly Distribution Chart
hist(df$TempAnomaly, 
     main = "Temperature Anomaly Distribution", 
     xlab = "Temperature Anomaly")

# Create a time series object
temp.ts <- ts(
  df$TempAnomaly,
  start = 1850,
  frequency = 1
)

# Time series plot
plot(
  temp.ts,
  type = "l",
  col = "blue",
  lwd = 2,
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Temperature Anomaly",
  main = "Northern Hemisphere Temperature Anomalies"
)

# Boxplot
boxplot(
  temp.ts,
  main = "Boxplot of Temperature Anomalies",
  col = "lightgreen"
)

# Moving Average plot
ma10 <- rollmean(temp.ts,
                 k = 10,
                 fill = NA)

plot(temp.ts,
     type = "l",
     main = "Temperature Anomalies with 10-Year Moving Average",
     ylab = "Temperature Anomaly",
     xlab = "Year")

lines(ma10,
      col = "red",
      lwd = 3)
```
ACF and PACF
```{r}
#Obtain the appropriate ACF and PACF plots, and use these to make a preliminary identification of a time series model.
# ACF and PACF charts
acf(temp.ts,
    main = "ACF of Temperature Anomalies")

pacf(temp.ts,
     main = "PACF of Temperature Anomalies")

temp.diff = diff(temp.ts) #we diff because the og data has strong trend and not stationary and ARIMA works best stationary

plot(
  temp.diff,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Change in Temperature Anomaly",
  main = "First-Differenced Temperature Anomalies")

acf(
  temp.diff,
  main = "ACF of Differenced Temperature Anomalies")

pacf(
  temp.diff,
  main = "PACF of Differenced Temperature Anomalies")
```

ARIMA Model Fitting
```{r}
#Fit an ARIMA model obtained via preliminary identification, and examine the residuals and their properties.

fit_prelim = Arima(
  temp.ts,
  order = c(0,1,2),
  method = "ML"
)

res_prelim =  residuals(fit_prelim)

# Residual time-series plot
plot(
  res_prelim,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Residual",
  main = "Residuals from Preliminary ARIMA Model"
)

abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

# Residual ACF
acf(
  res_prelim,
  main = "ACF of Preliminary-Model Residuals"
)

# Histogram
hist(
  res_prelim,
  main = "Histogram of Preliminary-Model Residuals",
  xlab = "Residual"
)

# Normal probability plot
qqnorm(
  res_prelim,
  main = "Normal Probability Plot of Preliminary-Model Residuals"
)

qqline(res_prelim)

checkresiduals(fit_prelim) #this is all for checking the properties of the residuals 
```

Selecting Final Model Using AIC
```{r}
#Select the final model using the model selection criterion AIC. 

#Create table for AIC values and each pq combination
aic.table = expand.grid(
  p = 0:3,
  q = 0:3)

#Placeholder Column for the AIC values 
aic.table$AIC = NA

#Fit each combination of model, compute AIC and put it in table
for (i in 1:nrow(aic.table)) {
  
  current.fit = tryCatch(
    Arima(
      temp.ts,
      order = c(aic.table$p[i], 1, aic.table$q[i]),
      method = "ML"),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  
  if (!is.null(current.fit)) {
    aic.table$AIC[i] = AIC(current.fit)
  }
}
aic.table #Please present a table with values of the criterion function you have used.

aic.table %>% #lowest AIC = final model
  filter(AIC == min(AIC)) #p=3, q=0, AIC=-193.52
#------------------------------------

# Fit the final model
final_model = Arima(
  temp.ts,
  order = c(3, 1, 0),
  method = "ML")

final_model
```

```{r}
#Perform the necessary diagnostics on the residuals of the final model 

res_final <- residuals(final_model)

# Residual time-series plot
plot(
  res_final,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Residual",
  main = "Residuals from Final ARIMA Model")

abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

# Residual ACF
acf(
  res_final,
  main = "ACF of Final-Model Residuals")

# Histogram
hist(
  res_final,
  main = "Histogram of Final-Model Residuals",
  xlab = "Residual")

# Normal probability plot
qqnorm(
  res_final,
  main = "Normal Probability Plot of Final-Model Residuals")

qqline(res_final)

# Ljung-Box test
Box.test(
  res_final,
  lag = 10,
  type = "Ljung-Box",
  fitdf = 3 + 0)

# Convenient combined residual diagnostic plot
checkresiduals(final_model)
```

```{r}
#Write down the final model, the estimated parameters and the standard errors.

final_model #ARIMA(3,1,0)

coef.table = data.frame(
  Estimate = as.numeric(final_model$coef),
  Standard_Error = sqrt(diag(final_model$var.coef)))

coef.table
```

```{r}
#Refit the final model 
train.ts = window(temp.ts, end = 2019)
test.ts = window(temp.ts, start = 2020)

fit_train = Arima(
  train.ts,
  order = c(3, 1, 0),
  method = "ML")

forecast_last6 = forecast(fit_train, h = 6)

forecast.table = data.frame( #made a table to compare actual and forecasted values
  Year = 2020:2025,
  Actual = as.numeric(test.ts),
  Forecast = as.numeric(forecast_last6$mean))

forecast.table
```

```{r}
#It is sometimes desirable to compare forecasting by different methods.

train_df = df[df$Year <= 2019, ] #from 1850-2019
test_df = df[df$Year >= 2020, ] #from 2020-2025

loess_fit = loess(TempAnomaly ~ Year, data = train_df)

summary(loess_fit)

train_df$Trend = fitted(loess_fit)

plot(
  train.df$Year,
  train.df$TempAnomaly,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Temperature Anomaly",
  main = "Temperature Anomalies and Fitted LOESS Trend")

lines(
  train.df$Year,
  train.df$Trend,
  col = "red",
  lwd = 3)

legend(
  "topleft",
  legend = c("Observed Temperature Anomaly", "LOESS Trend"),
  col = c("black", "red"),
  lty = 1,
  lwd = c(1, 3))

train.df$Rough = train.df$TempAnomaly - train.df$Trend

rough.ts = ts( #create ts object for rough
  train.df$Rough,
  start = 1850,
  frequency = 1)

plot( #rough against time
  rough.ts,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "Year",
  ylab = "Rough",
  main = "Rough After Removing the LOESS Trend")

abline(h = 0, lty = 2)

acf(rough.ts, main = "ACF of the Rough")

pacf(rough.ts, main = "PACF of the Rough")

#Same thing as above creating all possible cases for p and q between 0 and 3
arma.aic.table = expand.grid(
  p = 0:3,
  q = 0:3
)

arma.aic.table$AIC = NA

# Fit each ARMA(p, q) model to the rough
for (i in 1:nrow(arma.aic.table)) {
  
  current.fit <- tryCatch(
    Arima(
      rough.ts,
      order = c(
        arma.aic.table$p[i],
        0,
        arma.aic.table$q[i]
      ),
      method = "ML"
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  
  if (!is.null(current.fit)) {
    arma.aic.table$AIC[i] <- AIC(current.fit)
  }
}

arma.aic.table

lowest_rough_AIC = arma.aic.table %>% #best fit is p=1, q=0, AIC=-209.5037
  filter(AIC == min(AIC))

fit_rough_final = Arima(
  rough.ts,
  order = c(1,0,0),
  method = "ML")

fit_rough_final
```

```{r}
#Forecast the temperature anomalies for the years 2020-2025 by guessing the trend for these years

forecast_years = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)

trend.forecast.output = approxExtrap(
  x = train.df$Year,
  y = train.df$Trend,
  xout = forecast.years)

trend.forecast = trend.forecast.output$y

loess.arma.forecast = trend.forecast + as.numeric(rough.forecast$mean)

loess.arma.table = data.frame(
  Year = forecast.years,
  Extrapolated_Trend = trend.forecast,
  Forecasted_Rough = as.numeric(rough.forecast$mean),
  Forecasted_Anomaly = loess.arma.forecast,
  Actual_Anomaly = test.df$TempAnomaly)

loess.arma.table

comparison_table = data.frame(
  Year = forecast.years,
  Actual = test.df$TempAnomaly,
  ARIMA_Forecast = as.numeric(forecast_last6$mean),
  LOESS_ARMA_Forecast = loess.arma.forecast
)

comparison_table
```

```{r}
# Start forecast lines at 2019 so that they connect visually

)

)

)

)

lines(
  plot.years,
  loess.arma.plot.values,
  col = "red",
  lwd = 2,
  lty = 3
)

points(
  forecast.years,
  loess.arma.forecast,
  col = "red",
  pch = 15
)

legend(
  "topleft",
  legend = c(
    "Observed",
    "Direct ARIMA Forecast",
    "LOESS Trend + ARMA Rough Forecast"
  ),
  col = c("black", "blue", "red"),
  lty = c(1, 2, 3),
  pch = c(16, 17, 15),
  lwd = c(1, 2, 2)
)
```
